question:
Select the most appropriate one-word substitution of the given group of words.
Irreverent behaviour toward anything held sacred or concerning God.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Blasphemy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Blasphemy" means irreverent behaviour, speech, or action toward anything held sacred, especially God or religion. (ईश्वर-निंदा / धर्म का अपमान)
◦ Example: The preacher was accused of blasphemy after mocking the sacred scriptures.

• The word comes from the Greek blasphemia, meaning "evil speaking" or "slander", and in modern usage it specifically refers to disrespect shown toward religious beliefs or figures.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Agnosticism (अज्ञेयवाद): The belief that the existence of God or the divine is unknown or unknowable — it is a philosophical position, not an act of irreverence.

• Option 2: Pantheism (सर्वेश्वरवाद): The belief that God is identical with the universe, or that everything in the universe is a manifestation of God.

• Option 3: Theism (आस्तिकता): The belief in the existence of God or gods, especially a creator who is involved in the universe.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutions often asked in SSC: "Agnostic" (one who believes nothing can be known about God's existence), "Atheist" (one who does not believe in God), "Iconoclast" (one who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions), and "Heresy" (a belief contrary to established religious doctrine).

question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.
A. Many countries throughout the world have achieved full digitalisation.
B. Initially, the entire world transitioned to digitalisation.
C. This type of internet is known as a metaverse.
D. This existing kind of internet technology, which gives us access to various aspects, is about to change into a better and newer version.
E. The Metaverse is an intriguing technology that has been described as the 'newer version of the internet'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. DCEBA.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The paragraph must open with sentence D, which introduces the topic in general terms — the existing internet technology "is about to change into a better and newer version" — without depending on any earlier sentence for its meaning.

• Sentence C logically follows D because the pronoun phrase "This type of internet" in C directly refers back to the "better and newer version" mentioned at the end of D, and names it as the metaverse.

• Sentence E follows C and elaborates on the term just introduced, describing the Metaverse as "an intriguing technology... described as the newer version of the internet" — a natural expansion of the definition given in C.

• Sentences B and A then provide supporting background: B states that the world "initially" transitioned to digitalisation, and A concludes by noting that "many countries... have achieved full digitalisation", rounding off the paragraph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2, i.e. D-C-E-B-A.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (BCEDA) is incorrect because starting with B and then jumping to C ("This type of internet") leaves the pronoun "This" without any antecedent — the metaverse has not yet been introduced.

• Option 3 (ABCDE) is incorrect because it opens with a concluding-type statement (A) before the concept of digitalisation or the metaverse has even been introduced, breaking the logical flow.

• Option 4 (EADCB) is incorrect because starting with E introduces "the Metaverse" abruptly, and the shift to A (about digitalisation generally) immediately after has no logical connector.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the opening sentence first — it should introduce the topic without relying on pronouns like "this", "it", "such" that need an earlier antecedent.

• Next, look for linking words and pronouns ("this type", "this technology", "therefore") to chain the remaining sentences correctly.

• Practise identifying whether a sentence is a general/topic sentence, a supporting/example sentence, or a concluding sentence, as this helps quickly eliminate wrong sequences.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
Huge fire for celebration
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Bonfire.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Bonfire" is a large, open-air fire lit for celebration, signalling, or as part of a festive occasion. (उत्सव के लिए जलाई जाने वाली बड़ी आग)
◦ Example: Students gathered around the bonfire to celebrate the festival.

• The word originates from "bone fire" — historically a large fire in which bones were burned, later generalised to mean any large outdoor celebratory fire.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Firepower (गोलाबारी की क्षमता): The military capacity to deliver weaponised fire, i.e., the destructive capability of a weapon or force — unrelated to celebration.

• Option 2: Festivity (उत्सव): Refers to the celebration itself or an atmosphere of joyful celebration, not specifically to a fire.

• Option 3: Firefight (गोलीबारी): A battle or exchange of gunfire between opposing forces.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused fire-related one-word substitutions: "Conflagration" (a large destructive fire), "Incendiary" (a device designed to cause fire), "Pyre" (a heap of wood for burning a corpse), and "Inferno" (a large, uncontrollable fire).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
It is reported that she has win a prize money of ten lakhs at a reality show.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. she has won.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence describes an action (winning the prize) that happened at an unspecified past time but is relevant to the present report, which calls for the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense: Subject + has/have + V3 (past participle). The base sentence wrongly uses "has win", mixing the auxiliary "has" with the base form "win" instead of the past participle "won".

• Applying the rule: "she" (third person singular) takes "has", and the verb "win" must be changed to its past participle form "won", giving "she has won".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "she will won" is incorrect because it mixes the future auxiliary "will" with the past-tense form "won" instead of the base form; "will" must always be followed by V1 (e.g., "will win").

• Option 2: "she had win" is incorrect because the past perfect auxiliary "had" must be followed by the past participle "won", not the base form "win".

• Option 3: "No substitution required" is incorrect because the original phrase "she has win" is grammatically wrong — "has" (a perfect auxiliary) can never be followed by the base form of the verb.

NOTE

• The three forms of "win" are: win (V1) – won (V2) – won (V3); note that the past tense and past participle are identical.

• Common errors of this type in SSC exams involve confusing V1/V2/V3 after auxiliaries like has/have/had (Perfect tenses) and is/am/are/was/were (Passive voice / Continuous tense), so always check which verb form the auxiliary demands.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Joseph opened the Bible.
option_1: The Bible is being opened by Joseph.
option_3: The Bible was opened by Joseph.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The Bible was opened by Joseph.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Joseph opened the Bible" is an assertive sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the Bible" becomes the subject; since it is singular, the auxiliary used is "was"; the verb "opened" becomes the past participle "opened" (V3); and "Joseph" becomes the agent introduced with "by".
◦ Passive: The Bible was opened by Joseph.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "is being opened" is the passive form of the Present Continuous Tense, not the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it remains in the active voice (Present Continuous), and does not convert the sentence to passive at all.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it remains in the active voice (Simple Present Tense), and also changes the original past tense meaning of the sentence.

NOTE

• The verb "open" is a regular verb: open (V1) – opened (V2) – opened (V3).

• Remember that only transitive verbs (verbs that take an object) can be converted into the passive voice; intransitive verbs like "sleep", "arrive", "go" cannot normally be passivised.

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
He promised them / that he would sure repay / the loan urgently.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. that he would sure repay.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error lies in the use of "sure" as an adverb modifying the verb "repay". "Sure" is an adjective, not an adverb; the correct adverb form is "surely".

• Rule — Adjective vs. Adverb: An adjective qualifies a noun/pronoun, while an adverb qualifies a verb, adjective, or another adverb. Since "sure" here is meant to modify the verb "repay" (describing how he would repay), the adverb "surely" must be used, not the adjective "sure".

• Correction: "...that he would surely repay the loan urgently."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 (No error) is incorrect because the sentence does contain a grammatical error in part 4.

• Option 2 ("He promised them") is grammatically correct — a simple past-tense clause with a clear subject, verb and object.

• Option 3 ("the loan urgently") is grammatically correct — "urgently" is correctly used as an adverb modifying the verb "repay".

NOTE

• Common adjective–adverb confusion pairs frequently tested in SSC: sure/surely, hard/hardly, late/lately, near/nearly, high/highly, and most/mostly — each pair often carries a different meaning as well as a different grammatical role.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Gullible
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cynical.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Gullible" means easily deceived or tricked; too trusting. (आसानी से धोखा खा जाने वाला)
◦ Example: The gullible investor lost his savings to a fake scheme.

• "Cynical" means distrustful of people's motives; sceptical that people act from good or honest motives, which is the direct opposite of being easily deceived through excessive trust. (संशयवादी / लोगों पर अविश्वास करने वाला)
◦ Example: After being cheated twice, he became cynical about every new business proposal.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Credulous (भोला/विश्वासी): A near-synonym of "gullible" — willing to believe things too readily, not an antonym.

• Option 2: Pliant (लचीला): Easily influenced or bent to another's will — again closer in meaning to gullible than opposite to it.

• Option 4: Simple (सीधा-सादा): Can imply naivety, which is closer to the meaning of "gullible" rather than its opposite.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "gullible": naive, credulous, trusting, unsuspecting, easily fooled.

• Other antonyms of "gullible": sceptical, suspicious, wary, shrewd, distrustful.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The ball of yarn was being nudged by the kitten.
option_1: The kitten was nudged by the ball of yarn.
option_2: The kitten is nudging the ball of yarn.
option_3: The kitten was nudging the ball of yarn.
option_4: The kitten has been nudging the ball of yarn.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The kitten was nudging the ball of yarn.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The ball of yarn was being nudged by the kitten" is in the Past Continuous Tense, Passive Voice.

• Rule — Past Continuous Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + was/were + V-ing + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the kitten" becomes the subject; the auxiliary "was" is retained (kitten is singular); the past participle "nudged" is changed to the present participle "nudging"; and "the ball of yarn" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The kitten was nudging the ball of yarn.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because the subject and object have been interchanged wrongly, producing the illogical meaning that the kitten was nudged by the ball of yarn.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "is nudging" is the Present Continuous Tense, which does not match the original Past Continuous Tense.

• Option 4 is incorrect because "has been nudging" is the Present Perfect Continuous Tense, which also does not match the original Past Continuous Tense.

NOTE

• When converting Continuous Tense passives to active, remember the passive marker "being" is dropped in the active form, since "being + V3" only exists to show the action was ongoing while the object was subjected to it.

• Verb forms: nudge (V1) – nudged (V2) – nudged (V3).

question:
Select the most appropriate homonym of the underlined word to fill in the blank.
He was complimented for his appearance. His shirt ______ his trousers perfectly.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. complemented.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Complimented" (the underlined word) means praised or admired. (प्रशंसा की)

• Its homonym "complemented" means completed or went well together with, made something whole or perfect when combined. (पूरक बना / मेल खाया)
◦ Example: The scarf complemented her outfit beautifully.

• In the blank, "His shirt ______ his trousers perfectly" requires a verb meaning "matched/went well with", agreeing in tense with the first, past-tense clause of the sentence — this is "complemented", a homonym (same pronunciation) of "complimented" but with a different spelling and meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "competed" means took part in a contest — unrelated in sound and meaning to "complimented".

• Option 2: "complement" is the correct base form of the intended word but lacks the past-tense "-ed" ending needed to agree with the past-tense narrative set up by "He was complimented...".

• Option 3: "commented" means remarked or gave an opinion — again unrelated in sound to "complimented".

NOTE

• Complement vs. Compliment is a classic SSC homonym pair: "complement" = something that completes/matches; "compliment" = an expression of praise.

• Other common homonym pairs tested: stationary/stationery, principal/principle, affect/effect, council/counsel, desert/dessert.

question:
Select the correctly spelt option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
Patrrol is very costly these days.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Petrol.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Petrol" — a refined fuel derived from petroleum, used mainly to power vehicles.
◦ Example: The price of petrol has increased sharply this month.

• Spelling key: PET + ROL. Note there is only a single "t" and a single "r", and the word ends in "-rol", not "-role" or "-rul".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Petrole" — incorrect; an extra silent "e" has been wrongly added at the end.

• Option 2: "Petrul" — incorrect; the final vowel "u" is wrong, it should be "o".

• Option 3: "Patrole" — incorrect; the first vowel "a" is wrong (should be "e"), and it also carries the wrong extra "e" ending.

NOTE

• "Petrol" (British/Indian English) corresponds to "gasoline" or "gas" in American English.

• Related words with similar spelling patterns to watch for: petroleum, petroleum jelly, and the commonly confused non-word "patrol" (a verb/noun meaning to go around an area for security, which sounds different and is spelt differently from "petrol").

question:
Select the correctly spelt option that can substitute the underlined word in the given sentence.
The goods were taken on a public career.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. carrier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct word required here is "carrier" — a vehicle or vessel used for transporting goods or passengers, especially as a public conveyance.
◦ Example: The goods were shipped by a public carrier to the warehouse.

• Spelling key: CARR + IER — note the double "r" and the ending "-ier", not "-ryer" or a single "r".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "carier" — incorrect; it is missing the double "r".

• Option 2: "carryer" — incorrect; the correct spelling does not use "y" before the suffix.

• Option 4: "courier" — this is a correctly spelt, real word, but it means a person or company that delivers messages/packages, which is a different meaning from "carrier" (a public transport vehicle/vessel); it does not fit the given sentence.

NOTE

• Do not confuse "carrier" (a transport vehicle or a person/thing that carries something, e.g. "aircraft carrier", "disease carrier") with "courier" (a messenger who delivers parcels/documents) or "career" (a person's profession over their working life) — all three are frequently confused in SSC spelling and vocabulary questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
Is there any portal to redeem these coupons that I have collected from the store?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. forfeit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Redeem" here means to exchange (a coupon, voucher, etc.) for goods, cash, or a reward; to claim the value of something. (भुनाना / मूल्य के बदले प्राप्त करना)
◦ Example: You can redeem these points for a free gift.

• "Forfeit" means to lose or be deprived of something as a penalty or consequence, to give up the right to something, which is the direct opposite of claiming/redeeming its value. (जब्त करना / अधिकार खो देना)
◦ Example: If you don't use the coupon before the deadline, you will forfeit it.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: forsake (त्यागना): To abandon or give up a person or a habit — not specifically about losing a benefit or right through penalty.

• Option 2: deplore (निंदा करना): To express strong disapproval of something — unrelated in meaning to redeeming coupons.

• Option 4: embezzle (गबन करना): To steal or misappropriate money placed in one's trust — unrelated to the act of redeeming/losing a coupon's value.

NOTE

• Other meanings of "redeem": to save someone from sin/error (religious sense), or to make up for a fault ("redeem oneself").

• Other antonym pairs involving loss of rights/value often tested in SSC: claim/forfeit, retain/relinquish, acquire/forgo.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom/phrase in the given sentence.
Today, the country's nationalists rule the roost and hand out the jobs.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. To be in charge.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To rule the roost" means to be the dominant person in a group, to be in charge or have control over others. (प्रभुत्व रखना / सर्वेसर्वा होना)
◦ Example: In that department, the senior manager rules the roost.

• The idiom originates from the barnyard, where the dominant rooster controls the roost (the perch where birds settle for the night), symbolising authority and dominance over the rest of the flock.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: To be prejudiced (पक्षपाती होना): To hold a preconceived, unfair opinion about someone — a different idea unrelated to controlling others.

• Option 3: To save a criminal (अपराधी को बचाना): Not related to the idiom's meaning of dominance or authority.

• Option 4: To exploit someone (शोषण करना): Implies unfairly using someone for one's own benefit, which is close but not identical to simply "being in charge" — ruling the roost is about dominance/control, not necessarily exploitation.

NOTE

• Other idioms of power/authority often asked in SSC: "To call the shots" (to be in charge, to make the decisions), "To hold the reins" (to be in control), and "To have the upper hand" (to have an advantage/control over someone).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.
Keep someone at arm's length
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Avoid becoming friendly with someone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "To keep someone at arm's length" means to avoid becoming too close, friendly, or familiar with someone; to maintain a distant or formal relationship. (किसी से दूरी बनाए रखना)
◦ Example: After being betrayed once, she keeps all new colleagues at arm's length.

• The phrase evokes the literal image of keeping a person physically at the distance of an outstretched arm — close enough to acknowledge but far enough to remain guarded.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: Avoid playing with someone: Too literal and narrow; the idiom is about emotional/social distance in general, not specifically about play.

• Option 3: Being someone's enemy (शत्रु होना): Too strong — keeping someone at arm's length simply means maintaining distance, not active hostility or enmity.

• Option 4: Avoid becoming bitter with someone: Confuses the idiom with ideas of resentment; the idiom is about distance/familiarity, not bitterness.

NOTE

• Other idioms of distance/closeness often tested in SSC: "To give someone the cold shoulder" (to deliberately ignore someone), "To break the ice" (to initiate conversation and ease tension), and "To hit it off" (to become friendly with someone quickly).

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word given in the sentence.
The efforts will be ________________ (vain) if we do not submit the project report on time.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. useless.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Vain" (in this context) means having no effect or success; futile, fruitless, useless. (व्यर्थ / निष्फल)
◦ Example: All his efforts to convince her were in vain.

• "Useless" carries the same meaning of producing no result or being of no value, making it the most appropriate synonym in this sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: careless (लापरवाह): Means not paying enough attention, negligent — a different meaning from "futile/useless".

• Option 3: delightful (आनंददायक): Means highly pleasing or charming — the opposite in tone to the intended negative meaning of "vain".

• Option 4: sensible (समझदार): Means having or showing good sense, practical — again unrelated to the meaning of "vain" as futile.

NOTE

• "Vain" has another common meaning too: having excessive pride in one's appearance or achievements (conceited), as in "a vain person". Candidates must judge the intended sense from context.

• Other synonyms of "vain" (futile sense): fruitless, futile, pointless, ineffective, unsuccessful.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The patient looked __________ and tired.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Pale" means light in colour; having an unusually white or drained appearance, often used to describe someone looking unwell or fatigued.
◦ Example: She looked pale and tired after the long journey.

• The sentence describes the patient's physical appearance alongside "tired", so the adjective "pale" (whitish, drained-looking) is the only word that fits both grammatically and semantically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "pail" is a noun meaning a bucket — it does not fit grammatically as an adjective describing appearance.

• Option 3: "pall" as a noun means a cloth spread over a coffin, or (as a verb) to become boring/tiresome through familiarity — it does not fit the sentence.

• Option 4: "peel" means to strip off the outer skin/covering of something (e.g., of a fruit) — irrelevant to describing a person's complexion.

NOTE

• "Pale", "pail", "pall" and "peel" are commonly confused homophones/near-homophones in SSC vocabulary questions — always judge from the part of speech required (adjective/noun/verb) and the context of the sentence.

• Related word: "pallor" (noun) — an unusual paleness of the face, often indicating illness or fear.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Natwar was a fraudster who always tried to fooling others.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. deceive.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The original sentence wrongly uses the gerund form "tried to fooling", but the structure "tried to" must always be followed by the base form (infinitive) of the verb, not a gerund (V-ing).

• Rule: "try to" + V1 (base form) — e.g., "tried to go", "tried to help", "tried to deceive". The pattern "try to" + V-ing is grammatically incorrect.

• Among the options, only "deceive" is in the base verb form that correctly completes "tried to deceive others", and it also fits the meaning of a "fraudster" — one who deliberately misleads people.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "betraying" is a gerund form (V-ing), which is grammatically wrong after "tried to"; the correct base form would be "betray".

• Option 3: "cheating" is likewise a gerund form (V-ing), which does not correctly follow "tried to"; the correct base form would be "cheat".

• Option 4: "revealing" is also a gerund form (V-ing) and, in addition, its meaning (to disclose/expose) does not fit the context of a fraudster's intent, which should describe deceiving others, not revealing something to them.

NOTE

• The infinitive pattern "to + V1" is used after many common verbs like try, want, decide, plan, hope, agree, promise, refuse — none of these should be followed by a gerund (V-ing) form.

• Words related to deception frequently tested together in SSC vocabulary questions: deceive, dupe, con, swindle, defraud, hoodwink.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Consent
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Assent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Consent" means permission for something to happen; agreement to do something. (सहमति / अनुमति)
◦ Example: The doctor obtained the patient's consent before starting the treatment.

• "Assent" means the expression of approval or agreement; to agree to something, which conveys essentially the same meaning as "consent". (स्वीकृति देना)
◦ Example: The king gave his assent to the new law.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Avert (टालना): Means to prevent or ward off something (e.g., avert a disaster) — the opposite kind of meaning, unrelated to agreement.

• Option 3: Disturb (परेशान करना): Means to interfere with or upset the normal state of something — unrelated to agreement/permission.

• Option 4: Dissent (असहमति): Means to disagree or hold a different opinion — this is actually the antonym, not the synonym, of "consent".

NOTE

• Be careful not to confuse "assent" (agreement, pronounced like "consent") with "ascent" (the act of climbing/rising) — a classic homophone trap in SSC vocabulary questions.

• Other synonyms of "consent": agreement, approval, acquiescence, compliance, sanction.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A place to play games and bet on them
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Casino.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Casino" is a public place where people play games of chance for money, i.e., gambling games. (जुआघर)
◦ Example: Tourists flocked to the casino to try their luck at the tables.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Motel (मोटल): A roadside hotel designed for motorists, offering parking near the rooms — meant for lodging, not gambling.

• Option 2: Hotel (होटल): An establishment providing paid lodging, and sometimes food — again unrelated to games/betting.

• Option 4: Pub (मधुशाला/शराबखाना): An establishment licensed to sell alcoholic drinks for consumption on the premises — associated with drinking, not specifically with betting/gambling games.

NOTE

• Other place-related one-word substitutions frequently tested in SSC: "Sanatorium" (a place for treating chronic illness), "Orphanage" (a home for orphaned children), "Asylum" (a place of refuge/shelter, or a mental institution), and "Armoury" (a place where weapons are stored).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.
Karan call the restaurant / to ask if he could / reserve a table for tomorrow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Karan call the restaurant.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The error is one of Subject-Verb Agreement. "Karan" is a third-person singular subject, and in the Simple Present Tense a third-person singular subject must take a verb ending in "-s/-es".

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement (Simple Present): Third person singular subject + V1 + s/es. The sentence wrongly uses the bare base form "call" instead of "calls".

• Correction: "Karan calls the restaurant..."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 ("reserve a table for tomorrow") is grammatically correct — it correctly follows the infinitive structure "to ask if he could reserve...".

• Option 3 ("to ask if he could") is grammatically correct — "could" is properly used to express a polite possibility/permission within the reported clause.

• Option 4 ("No error") is incorrect because the sentence does contain an error, in part 1.

NOTE

• Common Subject-Verb Agreement errors tested in SSC involve singular third-person subjects (he/she/it, or a singular proper noun) taking a bare V1 instead of V1+s/es, especially in longer sentences where the subject and verb are separated by other phrases.

• Always identify the main subject and its corresponding main verb first, ignoring intervening phrases, to check agreement quickly.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1)________, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students' attention. Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. important.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank requires a word that logically leads into the explanation "...particularly for a teacher, to realise that students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers before you." This is presented as a significant point the teacher must keep in mind, so the sense required is "important" (i.e., it is important to realise this fact).

• The overall tone of the passage is instructional and advisory, guiding teachers on best practices — hence a word conveying significance/necessity of awareness, such as "important", fits naturally with the sentence's purpose.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "urgent" implies something requiring immediate action, which does not fit the reflective, advisory tone of "to realise" a general teaching principle.

• Option 2: "immaterial" means unimportant or irrelevant, which is the opposite of the intended meaning — the passage clearly treats this point as significant, not irrelevant.

• Option 3: "unnecessary" means not needed, which again contradicts the passage's intent of highlighting a point teachers should keep in mind.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the full passage first to grasp the overall tone (advisory, critical, celebratory, etc.) before choosing words for individual blanks — the surrounding sentences usually make the intended meaning unambiguous.

• Words of similar meaning to "important" often tested: significant, crucial, essential, vital, notable.

We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1)________, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students' attention. Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. before.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you." This means the students have had three or four teachers prior to the current teacher (i.e., before "you"), teaching them the same or related content.

• The word "before" here functions as a preposition meaning "earlier than; prior to", correctly indicating a sequence in time relative to the teacher being addressed.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "behind" indicates a position at the back of something (spatial), which does not fit the temporal/sequential sense required here.

• Option 2: "beside" means next to or alongside, a spatial preposition that does not convey the intended meaning of a preceding sequence of teachers.

• Option 4: "after" would reverse the intended meaning — it would suggest the three or four teachers came after "you", which contradicts the logical flow (the passage is explaining that students often tune out because they've already heard similar information repeatedly from earlier teachers).

NOTE

• Prepositions of time such as before, after, since, until, by are frequently tested in SSC cloze passages — always check whether the surrounding context indicates a sequence, a duration, or a deadline before selecting.

We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1)________, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students' attention. Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. come.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank appears in: "...will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them." The fixed idiomatic collocation here is "come alive", meaning to become lively, vivid, or engaging.
◦ Example: Good illustrations can make a textbook come alive for young readers.

• The phrase "come alive" is a standard English collocation used to describe something becoming vibrant or engaging, and it also logically pairs with "and stay that way" (i.e., remain lively) later in the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "stay" does not fit grammatically or idiomatically before "alive" in this context — "stay alive" would mean to remain living, which changes the intended meaning and also duplicates the later "stay that way".

• Option 2: "depart" means to leave or go away — it does not collocate with "alive" and makes no sense in context.

• Option 3: "go" does not form a standard collocation with "alive" in this sense ("go alive" is not idiomatic English, unlike "come alive").

NOTE

• Common English collocations with "come" frequently tested in SSC: come alive, come true, come across, come along, come into effect.

We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1)________, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students' attention. Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. realise.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand." The blank requires a verb meaning to understand or become aware of a fact, which is "realise".
◦ Example: Teachers must realise that not every student learns at the same pace.

• The structure "important thing to realise is that..." is a common way of introducing a fact the reader/listener should become consciously aware of, matching the advisory tone of the whole passage.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "guess" means to estimate or conjecture without full knowledge, which does not fit — the sentence states a definite fact, not something to be guessed.

• Option 2: "detect" means to discover or notice something hidden or hard to perceive (often through investigation), which is too narrow/technical a sense for this general advisory statement.

• Option 4: "decide" means to make a choice or reach a conclusion, which does not fit — the sentence is about becoming aware of a fact, not making a decision.

NOTE

• "Realise" (to become aware of/understand a fact) is often confused with "recognise" (to identify/acknowledge something already known) and "realize" (American spelling variant of the same word) — both are frequently tested in SSC vocabulary and cloze questions.

We must understand that people can process very little information presented orally. So, it is (1)________, particularly for a teacher, to realise that the students have sometimes listened to three or four teachers (2)________ you. So, the teacher must have props like notes, handouts and slides that will make the learning material (3)________ alive for the students and stay that way with them. A visual aid, a little movement or colour will get the students' attention. Another important thing to (4)________ is that long, complicated sentences spoken fast are simply too difficult for students to understand. It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank no. 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. advisable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "It is, therefore, (5)________ to use short sentences that make sense to them instantly." The passage throughout offers suggestions and best practices for teachers (using props, visual aids, simple language), rather than laying down strict rules, so the blank requires a word meaning "recommended, wise to do, a good idea", which is "advisable".
◦ Example: It is advisable to keep your explanations short and clear for young learners.

• The word "therefore" signals a logical conclusion drawn from the preceding advice about long, complicated sentences being hard to understand — a natural conclusion is a recommendation, not an absolute command.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "compulsory" means required by rule or law, which is too strong and does not match the advisory, suggestion-based tone of the passage.

• Option 3: "mandatory" similarly implies an obligatory requirement enforced by authority, which does not fit a passage offering teaching tips rather than binding rules.

• Option 4: "prohibited" means forbidden, which is the opposite of the intended meaning — the passage is recommending the use of short sentences, not forbidding it.

NOTE

• Distinguish between words expressing obligation (compulsory, mandatory, obligatory) and words expressing recommendation (advisable, recommended, preferable) — cloze passages often test this distinction based on the overall tone of the text (rule-based vs. advice-based).
